blocks.text: A professional yet approachable digital multimeter designed for everyday fault‑finding, commissioning, and learning. The CHY DT‑9205A combines a generous 1999‑count LCD with a tactile rotary selector, an audible continuity buzzer, diode mode, capacitance range (C×), and an hFE transistor socket for quick PNP/NPN checks. The front panel groups the four input jacks—10A, mA, COM, and VΩ—with clear silk‑screen icons so beginners plug in correctly on the first try. A rear kickstand improves viewing angle on benches, and the easy‑access battery door accepts a standard 9 V (6F22) cell. From hobby breadboards and classroom labs to appliance servicing and light industrial maintenance, the DT‑9205A focuses on the core measurements you need and removes unnecessary complexity.

جهاز ملتيميتر رقمي احترافي وسهل الاستخدام لعمليات تتبّع الأعطال، والتشغيل الأولي، والتعلّم اليومي. يجمع CHY DT‑9205A بين شاشة كبيرة 1999 خانة مع مفتاح دوّار مريح، وصفّارة استمرارية، ووضع اختبار الديود، ومدى قياس السعة (C×)، بالإضافة إلى مقبس hFE لاختبار ترانزستورات PNP/NPN بسرعة. تُرتَّب منافذ الإدخال الأربعة في الواجهة—10A وmA وCOM وVΩ—مع أيقونات واضحة كي يوصّل المبتدئ بالشكل الصحيح من المحاولة الأولى. يمنحك المسند الخلفي زاوية رؤية مريحة على الطاولة، كما يتيح غطاء البطارية الوصول السريع لاستخدام خلية 9 فولت (6F22) القياسية. من لوحات التجارب ومختبرات التعليم إلى صيانة الأجهزة المنزلية والصيانة الخفيفة، يركّز DT‑9205A على القياسات الأساسية ويُبعد التعقيد غير الضروري.

The DT‑9205A hits the sweet spot for technicians who need dependable readings without paying for boutique features. Its display is readable from across a bench, and the selector dial offers distinct detents that reduce accidental mis‑ranges. The dedicated 10 A jack supports short‑interval high‑current checks, while the mA jack—protected by an internal fuse—covers delicate circuits. A separate Cx socket measures common capacitors so you can verify power‑supply filters or troubleshoot motor run caps on site. The hFE socket lets you get a rough idea of transistor gain when sorting through parts bins or validating quick repairs. Combined with affordable test leads and a rugged case, the meter becomes an everyday tool you won’t hesitate to throw in a toolkit.

يقدّم DT‑9205A قيمة متوازنة لمن يبحث عن قراءات موثوقة دون دفع ثمن ميزات فاخرة نادرًا ما تُستخدم. تُقرأ الشاشة بوضوح من مسافة، ويمنحك القرص الدوّار نقرات ثابتة تحدّ من اختيار المدى بالخطأ. يدعم منفذ 10 A قياسات التيار العالي لفترات قصيرة، بينما يغطي منفذ mA—المؤمَّن بصمّام داخلي—الدوائر الحساسة. يوفر مقبس Cx قياس السعات الشائعة للتحقق من مرشّحات مزوّدات الطاقة أو تتبّع أعطال مكثّفات تشغيل المحركات في الموقع. أما مقبس hFE فيمنحك تقديرًا سريعًا لكسب الترانزستور عند فرز القطع أو التحقق من الإصلاحات السريعة. ومع مجسّات قياس اقتصادية وهيكل متين، يصبح الجهاز أداة يومية جاهزة دائمًا للحقيبة.

blocks.text: ESP8266 ESP‑01 12V 2‑Channel Wi‑Fi Relay Module (Dual Buttons) | وحدة تتابع واي فاي 12 فولت قناتان (زرّان)

The ESP8266 ESP‑01 12V 2‑Channel Wi‑Fi Relay Module combines an ESP‑01 (ESP8266) Wi‑Fi card with a stable STM8S103 MCU to deliver wireless control of two independent 10A relays. It supports two operating modes—Mode 1 (AP/direct) and Mode 2 (STA/router)—with dual buttons (S1 mode toggle, S2 factory reset), clear LED indicators for mode, status, and each relay, and screw terminals labeled COM1/NO1/NC1 and COM2/NO2/NC2. For makers and integrators, the board exposes UART TX/RX for ESP debugging and SWIM/NRST pads for the STM8. Typical direct AP range is ~100 m in open air; in router mode range depends on AP signal (some listings quote up to 400 m line‑of‑sight). Each relay is a SRD‑12VDC‑SL‑C rated 10A @ 250VAC or 10A @ 30VDC.

blocks.text: ESP8266 ESP‑01 12V 1‑Channel Wi‑Fi Relay Module (Dual Button) | وحدة تتابع واي فاي 12 فولت قناة واحدة (زِران)

This 12V single‑channel Wi‑Fi Relay Module combines an ESP‑01 (ESP8266) Wi‑Fi module with an STM8S103 microcontroller to deliver reliable wireless control of a 10A relay for smart‑home and workshop automation. The board exposes two operating modes (AP/direct and STA/router), two push buttons (S1 Mode switch, S2 Factory reset), rich LED indicators (status, mode, relay state), and screw terminals for safe mains/low‑voltage switching (COM/NO/NC). For developers, it retains UART (TX/RX) for ESP‑01 debugging and SWIM/NRST pads for STM8 programming. In open space the direct AP link reaches up to ~100 m, while router mode depends on the access‑point signal. The relay is the well‑known SRD‑12VDC‑SL‑C (10A@250VAC / 10A@30VDC). Android phones are supported for SmartConfig provisioning. When the ESP‑01 is unplugged, the board can act as a USB/TTL‑driven relay via the MCU (as a local/bench relay).

تجمع هذه الوحدة ذات القناة الواحدة بجهد 12 فولت بين وحدة ESP‑01 (ESP8266) للاتصال اللاسلكي ومعالج STM8S103 لتوفير تحكم موثوق في ريلاي 10 أمبير لأتمتة المنزل والورشة. تتضمن اللوحة وضعين للتشغيل (وضع نقطة الوصول المباشر AP، ووضع الراوتر STA)، وزرّين (S1 لتبديل الوضع، S2 لإرجاع المصنع)، ومجموعة لمبات بيان (حالة التشغيل، وضع العمل، حالة الريلاي)، وأطراف لولبية آمنة للتوصيل (COM/NO/NC). للمطورين، تتوافر واجهة UART (TX/RX) لتصحيح ESP‑01 ووسادات SWIM/NRST لبرمجة STM8. في بيئة مفتوحة قد يصل مدى الربط المباشر إلى ~100 متر، بينما يعتمد وضع الراوتر على قوة إشارة نقطة الوصول. الريلاي المستخدم هو SRD‑12VDC‑SL‑C الشائع (10A عند 250VAC أو 30VDC). يدعم إعداد الشبكة عبر Android/SmartConfig. وعند نزع ESP‑01 يمكن استخدام اللوحة كريلاي USB/TTL عبر المتحكم.

desc: Mini CN3065 solar/USB charger for single 3.7 V Li-ion/LiPo , up to 500 mA , inputs 4.4–6 V via Micro-USB or PH2.0 solar , SYS OUT power-path for running loads while charging, status CH/OK LEDs , tiny 39.8×20 mm PCB. وحدة شحن شمسية/USB CN3065 لخلية ليثيوم واحدة 3.7 فولت بتيار حتى 500 مللي أمبير ، دخل 4.4–6 فولت عبر مايكرو-USB أو موصل شمسي PH2.0 ، مخرج SYS OUT لتغذية الحمل أثناء الشحن مع LED لحالة الشحن ، بحجم صغير 39.8×20 مم .

blocks.text: CN3065 18650 Li-ion Mini Solar Charger Module

Ultra-compact solar/USB charger board based on CN3065 for single-cell 3.7 V Li-ion/LiPo (4.2 V full). It accepts 4.4–6 V from a small solar panel or Micro-USB 5 V, provides up to 500 mA charge current, and offers power-path “SYS OUT” so your load can run while the cell charges. On-board PH2.0-2P connectors simplify wiring and CH/OK LEDs show charging status.

وحدة شحن شمسية/USB فائقة الصغر مبنية على شريحة CN3065 لشحن خلية ليثيوم واحدة 3.7 فولت (4.2 فولت عند الامتلاء). تقبل دخل 4.4–6 فولت من لوح شمسي صغير أو مايكرو-USB 5 فولت، مع تيار شحن حتى 500 مللي أمبير، وتدعم مخرج SYS OUT لتغذية الحمل أثناء الشحن. موصلات PH2.0-2P تسهّل التوصيل، ولمبتا CH/OK تعرضان حالة الشحن.

blocks.text: USB Solar Panel Charging Controller Module 5V 2A

Compact DC-DC solar-to-USB buck module that converts a small solar panel’s output to a regulated 5V/2A USB supply for charging phones, power banks, and powering USB gadgets (fans, lamps, micro-controllers). The board accepts a low-power panel (e.g., 12V / 10W ) and provides a stable USB-A output with high-efficiency switching and clear polarity markings on the input pads. Indoor use is recommended (not waterproof).

blocks.text: A compact MPPT solar charging board for a single 3.7V Li-ion/LiPo cell. Now fully documented with indicator behavior, switching frequency, thermal range, and charge algorithm details. Size 44.8 × 20 mm, dual PH2.0-2P connectors both sides, and rear pads to select 5V/6V/9V/12V panel presets. [Updated] Includes LED status (CH/OK), ~300 kHz PWM switching, auto-recharge & soft-start, and –40 to +85 °C operating range .

لوحة شحن شمسي MPPT لخلية ليثيوم 3.7 فولت واحدة، مع توثيق كامل لسلوك لمبات البيان، وتردد التبديل، ونطاق الحرارة، وتفاصيل خوارزمية الشحن. الأبعاد 44.8 × 20 مم، وموصلات PH2.0-2P مزدوجة على الجهتين، ووسائد خلفية لاختيار جهد اللوح 5/6/9/12 فولت. [تحديث] تتضمن حالة اللمبات (CH/OK)، وتبديل ~300 كيلوهرتز، وإعادة شحن تلقائية وبداية لينة، ونطاق تشغيل –40 إلى +85 °م .

✅ Up to ~2 A charge with R050 sense (panel & thermal permitting). [Updated] Rated in file.
✅ CC/CV algorithm with 4.2 V constant-voltage target for Li-ion cells. [Updated] 4.2 V CV set-point noted.
✅ Auto-recharge & soft-start for safe recovery and smooth engagement. [Updated]
✅ ~300 kHz PWM switching for compact magnetics and low ripple. [Updated]
✅ Wide ambient range –40 °C…+85 °C for outdoor nodes. [Updated]
✅ MPPT حقيقي لإخراج طاقة أعلى مقارنة بالشواحن الخطية.
✅ اختيار جهد اللوح من الخلف: 5/6/9/12 فولت لملاءمة الألواح الصغيرة.
✅ تيار شحن حتى ~2 أمبير مع R050 (وفق قدرة اللوح وإدارة الحرارة). [تحديث] قيمة مذكورة في الملف.

A robust 20A PWM solar charge controller for small off-grid systems. It auto-detects 12V/24V, drives 20A charge & 20A load, shows real-time status on a backlit LCD, offers dual 5V USB, selectable lighting/timer modes, and full electrical protections. Updated technical limits from the unit’s datasheet are included below for accurate system sizing.

✅ LCD + keys for clear PV/Battery/Load icons, voltage readouts, and quick parameter edits.
✅ Dual USB 5V (~2A shared) for phones and small gadgets.
✅ Load output modes: Manual ON/OFF, Dusk-to-Dawn, Timer (1–24 h).
✅ Smart protections: reverse polarity, short-circuit, over-current/over-voltage, over-discharge, night reverse flow.
✅ Compact ABS body with side ears for simple wall/plate mounting.
✅ PWM 20 أمبير مع تعرّف تلقائي 12/24 فولت—مناسب لأنظمة بطاريات 12 أو 24 فولت عندما يكون Isc/Imp ≤ 20A وVoc ≤ 55 فولت.
✅ شاشة LCD وأزرار لرموز الشمس/البطارية/الحمل وقراءات الجهد وتعديل الإعدادات بسرعة.

blocks.text: MECHANIC AD‑223 Flux Paste 10ml (Syringe Kit with Applicator & Tips)

MECHANIC AD‑223 Flux Paste 10ml is a versatile, mildly‑activated rosin paste engineered for precision PCB rework and micro‑soldering. The 10‑millilitre syringe delivers controllable dots on IC pins, FPC seats and pad arrays, while the paste’s balanced activation window promotes fast wetting, bright joints and minimal spatter. Whether you are drag‑soldering fine‑pitch packages, wicking bridges or touching up oxidized pads, AD‑223 helps flux the surface, dissolve oxides, improve flow and shorten dwell time—all with residues that clean easily in IPA or dedicated PCB cleaners.

The retail kit typically includes the prefilled 10 ml syringe, a manual plunger/pusher rod and dispense tips (fine‑gauge, colour may vary by batch). Images show the familiar green sleeve with FLUX PASTE branding and “Alliance Design” livery—commonly found on mobile‑repair benches, laptop service centres and training labs.
✅ Controlled application — The syringe format lets you place a film or micro‑dot exactly where needed without flooding nearby components.
🔥 Fast wetting, glossy fillets — Active rosin chemistry speeds oxide removal and promotes smooth flow, so solder forms concave fillets instead of dull blobs.
🧼 Residues wipe off — Post‑reflow residues are removable with isopropyl alcohol (IPA) or PCB cleaners; many joints look neat even without a full wash.
🧯 Temperature‑friendly — Works reliably around common tip settings (approx. 300–360 °C); useful on both leaded (Sn60/63) and lead‑free alloys.
🧰 Multi‑role — Ideal for drag soldering, reballing assist, pad retinning, wire‑to‑pad work, and wicking bridges cleanly.
🧪 Consistency — Paste viscosity holds shape on vertical edges yet spreads thinly under heat for uniform coverage.
SMD rework: TSSOP/QFP/SOIC drag soldering; dot on the first and last pins, then sweep.
Connector service: FPC seats and tight board‑to‑board connectors; apply a hairline film to pin rows.
Pad revival: Retin dull/oxidized pads before placing jumpers or replacement parts.
Bridge cleanup: Add a tiny amount, then wick; flux lowers surface tension so bridges lift in a single pass.
Reballing support: Helps hold balls in place and improves wetting during reflow on small packages.
Through‑hole assist: On shield tabs and ground lugs, the paste accelerates heat transfer and reduces dwell time.
🔧 Less is more: A thin film usually outperforms a large blob. Excess flux can brown or bubble and trap contaminants.
🧽 Mind the cleanup: If the board must be pristine (optical paths, sensors), finish with IPA + lint‑free swabs.
🌡️ Tune temperature: Start around 330–350 °C for leaded work; raise slightly for heavy ground planes; drop for delicate pads.
🧲 Match solder wire: Pair with 0.3–0.5 mm leaded wire for fine‑pitch or 0.6–0.8 mm where pads are larger.
🧴 Storage discipline: Cap tightly; store cool and dry. Avoid prolonged exposure to hot benches or direct sunlight to preserve activity.

blocks.text: MECHANIC IR14ET Electric Glue Remover (Intelligent 6‑Speed, F/R, Type‑C, 2000mAh)

The MECHANIC IR14ET Electric Glue Remover is a precision, motorized pen for OCA/adhesive removal on smartphone and tablet displays. With intelligent 6‑speed control, forward/reverse rotation, and a high‑visibility green LED dust/illumination lamp, IR14ET gives repair pros uniform, low‑stress degumming on curved edges, hard adhesive lines, and narrow FPC seats—without overheating or jolting sensitive glass and flex tails. A robust 3.7V / 2000mAh lithium battery, Type‑C charging, and up to ≈10 hours of claimed endurance make it a dependable bench and field tool.

This page is based on the product cards you shared and package highlights (6‑speed, F/R, green LED, Type‑C, 2000mAh, ≈7000 rpm max, ≈15 W). Where a supplier didn’t specify exact values, we present safe, service‑tested practices and clearly mark typical/assumed items.
✅ Six intelligent speeds — Smooth 6‑gear adjustment for delicate film work through heavy residue without torque jumps.
🔁 Forward / Reverse — Instant direction change to pull residue away from flex cables or into catch zones; symmetric control around corners.
💡 Green Dust Display Lamp — Front‑end ultra‑light LED reveals dust and edge shadows for stress‑free positioning and night‑friendly maintenance.
🌀 No judder — One‑piece coaxial degumming shaft is tightly fixed at the motor center to maintain excellent concentricity and reduce operational errors.
🔥 Not hot / Not crash — Drive and thermal design resist overheating and stalling during long sessions.
🔋 Ultra‑long life — Internal 3.7V 2000mAh cell with efficiency logic; messaging targets ≈10 hours of continuous operation.
🧴 Solvent‑less capable — Efficient mechanical removal means you can work without chemical potions in many cases; optional IPA wipe for final finish.

blocks.text: MECHANIC SW-5S Tin-Dragging Needle (Gold-Plated, Anti-Static Carbon Handle) — Set with 5 Pins

A precision tin-dragging and micro-alignment tool designed for modern connector work, reballing assistance, and ultra‑fine solder control. The SW‑5S couples a pure‑copper, gold‑plated ball‑head needle with a featherweight, anti‑static carbon‑fiber handle. This balanced pairing glides across pad edges, nudges solder beads exactly where you want them, and reduces the chance of scratching solder mask or copper foil when working around FPC seats, card slots, and dense fine‑pitch interfaces.

✅ Gold‑plated pure‑copper tip — The copper core conducts heat away from hotspots; the gold surface resists oxidation and offers low friction, so solder pearls follow the tip smoothly without sticking.

✅ Ball‑head geometry — The small spherical tip fits connector gaps cleanly. It lets you sweep, herd, and align solder beads along the pad line, ideal for FPC seat welding, SIM/battery slot work, and post‑reflow grooming.
✅ Anti‑static carbon handle — ESD‑aware, ultra‑light, and warm to the touch. The matte carbon shaft limits static buildup while the knurled metal collet locks tips securely and allows quick swaps.
✅ Five replaceable needles — The set ships with 5 pcs ball‑head pins, so you can rotate tips as they age or dedicate each to different flux chemistries.
✅ Uniform, fast tinning — The surface finish and geometry help you spread solder evenly, preventing lumpy joints and saving time during connector alignment.
🔌 FPC connectors and inline seats — Align blades, pre‑form tin traces, and guide beads into uniform rows before locking the seat.
📱 Smartphone and tablet service — Arrange solder around USB‑C, audio jacks, SIM trays, and battery terminals without nicking the mask.
🧠 BGA edge assistance — During reballing or after reflow, sweep stray solder spheres away from keep‑out zones and into capture pads.
🪛 Component lead grooming — Tame bridges after drag‑soldering SOIC/TSSOP pins, then wick once for a clean, professional finish.
🧩 Prototype finishing — When paste deposits aren’t perfect, redistribute solder to even out pad‑to‑pad coverage.

Reset often. If the ball picks up solder, tap it on brass wool or a silicone mat; the gold surface cleans quickly.

blocks.text: Mechanic DS6 Solder Wire 0.4mm 40g (Sn60/Pb40, Rosin Core)

Mechanic DS6 Solder Wire 0.4mm 40g is engineered for makers, repair pros, and training labs that demand predictable flow, bright joints, and clean boards. This leaded alloy with a rosin core blends high wettability with thermal stability, so you can land a shiny fillet on the first pass instead of reworking the same pad twice. Whether you’re dragging across a row of SMD pins or feeding precisely into a through‑hole, the slim filament keeps control in your fingertips. The label highlights a flux content between 1.0–3.0%, traces of chloride under 0.05% in the flux, and messaging about low smoke, low splash, and no‑residue behavior, which lines up with the day‑to‑day reality of tidy, reliable electronics soldering.
✅ Fine‑pitch control — The 0.4 mm diameter feeds like pencil lead, letting you dose a pad without flooding nearby pads or jumpers.
🔥 Consistent wetting — The Sn60/Pb40 alloy has a forgiving melting window and a stable surface tension, so it pulls into a curved, concave fillet that looks right and conducts reliably.
🧪 Rosin core built in — The active rosin formulation inside the wire breaks oxides quickly and keeps the melt pool tidy with minimal spatter, giving you faster joints under normal bench temperatures.
🧼 Clean finish — Residual flux wipes easily with isopropyl alcohol; many boards look presentable right off the iron, especially when heat is controlled and the tip is properly tinned.
🧯 Thermal headroom — DS6 handles the typical 320–360 °C tip range well, letting you work across thin sensor pads and heavier ground pours with only modest temperature tweaks.
🛠️ Everyday reliability — A 40 g spool balances compact size with meaningful capacity for classrooms, field kits, and small production runs.
🎯 Repeatable results — Flux percentage printed on the label means predictable activity from spool to spool when you’re training new hands or building process sheets.
What you can build with Mechanic DS6 Solder Wire 0.4mm 40g
✅ SMD rework that looks factory — Drag solder SOICs, clean bridges with wick, and leave a row of pins bright and even.
✅ Sensor and module wiring — Land thin enamel wire on tiny pads without drowning test points; the 0.4 mm feed helps you control the puddle.
✅ Connector touch‑ups — Reinforce headers, jumpers, and switch tabs in consumer electronics; low splash keeps housings clean.
✅ Education and training — Students see instant wetting feedback and learn to read the concave fillet, not just the shine.
✅ Field repairs — The 40 g spool drops in a pouch; rosin core means fewer bottles on the bench when you’re traveling light.
✅ Prep the tip — Wipe on brass wool or a damp sponge and re‑tin immediately; a bright tip transfers heat, wets faster, and protects pads from prolonged heating.
✅ Aim for a concave fillet — Feed only until the solder forms a curved meniscus that hugs the pad and lead; if you see a ball, you fed too much.
✅ Stabilize small parts — Use tweezers, tape, or a dab of solder paste to hold tiny components; then feed DS6 to finish the joint in a single, confident move.
✅ Mind the copper mass — Bump tip temperature a little when you hit ground planes; drop back for delicate pads so the flux doesn’t over‑cook.
✅ Finish clean — If you need pristine boards, a quick IPA wipe removes rosin traces and leaves that crisp, professional look.

blocks.v: High wettability, thermal stability, low smoke, low splash

blocks.text: ✅ Irons — Temperature‑controlled stations with fine tips excel; conical or hoof tips let you choose between point dosing and drag soldering.
✅ Flux — The rosin core is enough for most work; for stubborn pads add a touch of no‑clean or RMA gel and let DS6 carry the rest.
✅ Wick — Pair with fine copper braid to lift bridges; DS6 replenishes pins after cleanup without over‑feeding.
✅ Magnification — A small visor makes 0.4 mm shine by reducing hand overshoot and improving angle control.
✅ Cleaning — Keep IPA and lint‑free swabs nearby; a single swipe returns the board to a professional finish.
🧯 Lead warning — Contains lead; wash hands after use and keep food and drinks off the bench.
🧤 Ventilation — Use fume extraction or at least a fan; even low‑smoke rosin benefits from airflow.
🧪 Storage — Keep the spool bagged away from dust; store cool and dry so the flux core stays active.
🧰 ESD awareness — When working on sensitive modules, bond your wrist to ground; DS6 won’t save a zapped gate.

✅ Is Mechanic DS6 Solder Wire 0.4mm 40g good for drag soldering? Yes—pair a hoof tip, wet the tip with a small bead, and slide along the pins. The rosin core refreshes the bead as you go; follow with a light wick pass if needed.
✅ Do I need extra flux? The rosin core is sufficient most of the time. For oxidized pads or heavy copper, a tiny dab of no‑clean gel accelerates the wetting and reduces dwell time.
✅ What temperature should I pick? Start around 340 °C and adjust for the board’s thermal mass. The right temperature is the lowest that completes the joint in two to three seconds.
✅ Will it leave residue? Rosin leaves a light film that often looks fine; if you want perfectly clean boards, wipe with isopropyl alcohol.
✅ Can I use DS6 on battery tabs or large chassis? Those require higher heat and different alloys. DS6 excels on electronics pads; for heavy tabs, use a wider tip and consider specialty solders.
سلك لحام Mechanic DS6 قطر 0.4 مم وزن 40 جم (Sn60/Pb40 مع فلكس روزن داخلي)

سلك Mechanic DS6 قطر 0.4 مم وزن 40 جم صُمّم لمن يبحث عن تدفّق متوازن ونتيجة لامعة ولوحة نظيفة من أول محاولة. السبيكة الرصاصية Sn60/Pb40 تمنحك نافذة انصهار مريحة وسطحًا يتشكّل بسهولة إلى فيليه مقعّرة متناسقة، فيما يقوم فلكس الرّوزن الداخلي بإزالة الأكسدة بسرعة ويحدّ من التناثر والدخان. بفضل القطر الرفيع يمكنك تغذية البادّات الصغيرة بدقة، وتثبيت الأسلاك الرقيقة، وسحب قصدير متحكّم به على صفوف أرجل الدوائر المتكاملة. تُظهر الملصقات نسبة فلكس بين 1.0–3.0% مع نسبة كلوريد في الفلكس لا تتجاوز 0.05%، مع عبارات عن ترطيب عالٍ وثبات حراري ودخان أقل وبقايا قليلة—وهي سمات تلائم عمل الصيانة والهواة والتعليم.

blocks.text: Meet Imax B3 3×800mA, the compact AC balance charger trusted for quick, safe charging of 2S–3S LiPo packs via JST-XH balance ports only. With three independent 800 mA balance channels, tri-color LEDs, and worldwide 100–240 V AC input, it’s the no-fuss companion for park flyers, RC cars, drones, and classrooms that need reliable charging without menus or setup.
✅ Focus on simplicity: Plug AC, connect the pack’s JST-XH balance lead, and the B3 handles CC/CV charging and cell balancing automatically.
🔌 Direct AC input (100–240 V): No external power brick; perfect for field boxes and makerspaces.
⚡ 3×800 mA balance output: Up to 0.8 A per cell (typical ~10 W total), ideal for 2S/3S packs from 800–2200 mAh.

🛡️ Multiple protections: Over-voltage, short-circuit, reverse-polarity, and thermal safeguards.
🧩 RC-friendly connectors: 3-pin (2S) and 4-pin (3S) JST-XH sockets built in—no adapters for common packs.
🧳 Compact & light: Toss it in your field bag; rubber feet keep it steady on the bench.
🔁 Balanced every cycle: Helps extend pack life and keep cells within tight delta-V thresholds.
🛠️ Hassle-free: No settings, no charge leads—just balance charge and go.
Note: B3 series charges via balance port only (no main lead). For 4S+ or adjustable rates, pick a programmable charger.

blocks.text: Meet the dependable high-capacity pack that delivers serious current without drama. The LiPo 11.1V 10400mAh 40C configuration balances runtime, punch, and compactness for demanding builds that need clean power on tap. From mobile robotics to field instruments and FPV ground systems, this pack is designed to supply a steady bus at 3S nominal while handling aggressive transient loads with low sag.
✅ High energy + stable bus — 11.1V nominal (3S) with ~115.4Wh of stored energy (10.4Ah × 11.1V) to extend missions and sessions without frequent swaps.

⚡ Serious discharge headroom — 40C continuous translates to up to 416A potential current (theoretical; size wiring and protection accordingly) to cover spikes from motors, RF finals, DC-DC inrush, and servo bursts.
🧠 Pack intelligence ready — Simple two-lead main output plus a balance header for cell-level maintenance and health checks with common hobby-grade chargers and analyzers.
🔒 Safety-first design practice — Robust shrink wrap, cell spacing, and vent path planning recommended in the bay; label windows allow quick identification for field crews and pilots.
🧰 Integration friendly — Fits typical 3S rails and power trees; easy to pair with 5V/12V buck converters, telemetry modules, and smart BMS add-ons.
🛠️ Serviceable lifecycle — Routine balance charging and storage-voltage discipline help preserve capacity across seasons.
🌡️ Thermal resilience workflow — Plan airflow around the pack; add temperature probes near the core during system validation to keep cell temps in the green under peak draw.
🔄 Repeatable deployment — Color-coded leads, protective caps, and strap-through mounting points support fast changeovers on carts, rigs, and drones.
🔌 Autonomous mobile robots (AMR/UGV) — Smooth supply for motor controllers, compute modules, depth cams, and radios.
🎥 Cine/field rigs — Feed monitors, wireless video, encoders, and follow-focus with a compact 3S bus and external regulators.
🛰️ Comms & test benches — RF amplifiers, SDR front-ends, and field diagnostics where a quiet DC source matters.
🚤 Surface/air RC platforms — Boats, planes, and large gliders that prefer 3S with plenty of surge capacity for takeoff and maneuvers.
🧪 STEM / lab builds — Capstone power plants for cap-rail experiments, mechatronics, and embedded systems.
✅ Wire gauge & connectors — Size main leads for worst-case continuous current with margin; keep harness runs short to minimize voltage drop.
✅ Mounting — Use wide straps or foam rails; avoid hard edges and fastener heads that can abrade the wrap under vibration.
✅ Redundancy — For mission-critical platforms, consider parallel packs with diodes or ideal-OR controllers and per-leg fusing.
✅ Telemetry — Add voltage and temperature telemetry on-board; set alerts conservatively to protect cells under dynamic loads.
✅ Balance discipline — Balance-charge regularly; investigate any cell that lags by >30–50mV after a proper rest period.
⚠️ Charge in a fire-resistant enclosure on a non-flammable surface; never leave unattended.
⚠️ Use a compatible balance charger set to 3S LiPo chemistry and correct capacity settings; inspect leads before connecting.
⚠️ Storage around 3.75–3.85V per cell for extended shelf life; check monthly and top up if needed.
⚠️ Temperature — Avoid charging below 0 °C or above 45 °C; keep operation within a sensible thermal envelope.
⚠️ Physical integrity — Retire packs that show swelling, puncture, odor, or recurring imbalance.
Energy: ~115.4 Wh provides, for example, ~2.3 hours at 50 W or ~1.0 hour at 110 W (not accounting for converter losses).
Current headroom: 40C on 10.4Ah → 416A theoretical; design continuous draw far lower with appropriate protection and thermal design.
Converters: Pair with high-efficiency buck/boost modules for 5V, 9V, or 12V rails; validate transient response with your load profile.
Balance lead: 3S balance header (typical for cell maintenance)
Basic use & care label: Quick reminders for charge, storage, and disposal
For best results, log per-cycle capacity, IR, and peak temps; trend these to make proactive replacement decisions in fleets.
🧷 Securement — Dual straps, non-slip mat, and corner padding.
🧯 Containment — Add a fire-resistant sleeve or bay partition in sensitive platforms.
🔁 Connect-disconnect routine — Power down loads before removing the pack; avoid arcing on high-current connectors.
🧪 Bring-up tests — Step-load testing from idle to surge; record bus sag and pack temps to set thermal limits.
🧲 EMI hygiene — Twist high-current pairs; route away from sensors/radios; add LC filtering if needed.
Fast voltage drop under load → Check harness resistance, connector health, and cell balance.
Charger won’t start → Verify balance plug seating and correct 3S profile.
Warm pack at light loads → Evaluate airflow and conversion losses; test for a weak cell.
Early cutoff → Confirm cutoff thresholds in ESC/BMS and recalibrate fuel-gauge assumptions.
♻️ Discharge to a safe level and follow local e-waste procedures. Isolate terminals.

blocks.text: Arduino Leonardo — ATmega32U4 Board with Native USB HID, 20 I/O, 7 PWM

Meet Arduino Leonardo—the classic 5 V development board built around the ATmega32U4 with native USB. Unlike boards that rely on a separate USB-to-serial chip, Leonardo talks USB directly, so it can appear to your computer as a keyboard, mouse, gamepad, MIDI device, or a virtual COM port—all from your sketch. This makes it a favorite for human-interface projects, creative controllers, automation, data-logging, and STEM classrooms where rapid iteration matters.

blocks.text: 2UUL DA12 MicroFix Hook – Underfill & Adhesive Removal Set

The 2UUL DA12 MicroFix Hook – Underfill & Adhesive Removal Set is purpose-built for precision cleanup around BGA packages and fine-pitch components on smartphone and electronics PCBs. This Underfill Removal Set combines an ultralight carbon-fiber holder with three specialized blades to lift cured underfill and scrape adhesive without stressing pads or solder joints. Its low mass, rigid handle, and sharp, controlled tips give technicians confident access in crowded board layouts while maintaining delicate control during rework.

Whether you’re preparing a board for IC replacement or removing stubborn bond adhesives around modules, the DA12’s quick blade changes and refined tip geometry streamline your workflow and help protect substrates, mask, and nearby components during critical stages of repair.

blocks.text: The Automatic Smart Car Battery Charger 10A 12/24VDC is a fixed-output automotive charger designed to charge and maintain 12 V and 24 V lead-acid batteries with a maximum charge current of 10 A (device-dependent). It’s aimed at cars, small vans, motorcycles (12 V systems), light equipment with 24 V banks, and workshop benches that standardize on lead-acid chemistry. The automatic logic manages bulk/absorption/float behavior so you can connect, confirm polarity, and let the charger complete the cycle without constant monitoring.
✅ Automatic charge logic — hands-off charging for 12 V and 24 V lead-acid batteries with staged progression to a maintenance level.
🔌 12 V / 24 V selection — supports common vehicle systems; check and match your battery voltage before connecting.
⚡ Up to 10 A class — practical current for everyday charging and top-ups within the intended battery size range.
🛡️ Basic charger protections — polarity attention, sensible connection sequence, and staged charge behavior support safer use.
🧩 Workshop convenience — straightforward clamps-to-terminals workflow for periodic maintenance or storage charging.
✅ Vehicles parked for long periods — recover and maintain 12 V starter batteries (capacity-appropriate).
✅ Workshop/garage — routine charging of customer batteries before diagnostics.
✅ Light equipment — 24 V systems that need periodic top-ups (e.g., small machinery with dual 12 V batteries in series).
✅ Seasonal gear — motorcycles, ATVs, or small boats (12 V) before first use of the season.
✅ Confirm battery type & voltage — use with lead-acid batteries at 12 V or 24 V only; match the selected mode to your battery bank.

✅ Size the current to the battery — as a rough rule of thumb for lead-acid, a charge rate around ~10% of Ah capacity is common; 10 A suits mid-sized 12 V batteries (example guidance only—follow your battery’s label).
✅ Connection order — connect clamps to the battery first (positive to +, negative to − on the correct post), then power the charger; disconnect in reverse order.
✅ Ventilation — charge in a ventilated space away from flames/sparks; lead-acid charging can release gas.
✅ Monitor initial minutes — verify correct mode/voltage and stable operation; avoid charging damaged or frozen batteries.
✅ Storage/maintenance — after reaching full charge, the maintenance/float behavior helps mitigate self-discharge during storage intervals.
✅ Battery chemistry: lead-acid (flooded/AGM/gel as specified by your battery manufacturer).
✅ Battery voltage: 12 V or 24 V (do not connect to other voltages).
✅ Battery condition: casing intact, terminals clean, no bulging/leaks; temperature within the battery’s recommended charge range.
🛡️ Polarity — always verify +/− before energizing; incorrect polarity can damage the system.
🔌 Secure clamps — ensure firm contact on clean terminals; avoid loose connections that can heat.
🌬️ Ventilate — keep the area clear; don’t cover the charger or battery during operation.
⚠️ No ignition sources — keep away from sparks, cigarettes, or open flames.
🧯 Supervise — do not leave charging unattended in unsuitable environments.

desc: 1.8 inch TFT LCD ST7735S 128×160 — compact color display with SPI-style interface, ST7735S controller, 16-bit RGB565 mode, and typical pins (VCC, GND, SCLK, MOSI, DC, CS, RST, LED) for easy integration. شاشة 1.8 بوصة TFT ST7735S بدقة 128×160 — عرض ملوّن مدمج بواجهة تسلسلية من نوع SPI، ومتحكّم ST7735S، ووضع لون 16-بت RGB565، مع أطراف نموذجية لدمج سريع.

blocks.text: The 1.8 inch TFT LCD ST7735S 128×160 module is a compact, color display driven by the ST7735S controller, widely used in maker projects, embedded UI panels, meters, and handheld devices. It presents a 128 × 160 pixel active-matrix TFT panel and communicates over a serial interface (SPI family), making it easy to wire with common microcontrollers and single-board computers. The controller natively supports color graphics with standard command sets used by popular graphics libraries, enabling quick bring-up and reliable rendering for icons, text, and simple animations.
✅ Proven controller — ST7735S is a stable, well-documented controller used across many 1.8″ TFTs, with a standard command set and dependable initialization flows.
🎨 Vivid color — supports full-color modes; most libraries use 16-bit RGB 565 for 65K colors, while the controller can also support 18-bit color addressing.
🔌 Serial interface friendly — works with SPI-style connections, minimizing pin count while keeping updates responsive for small UIs.
🧩 Broad library support — readily driven by widely used frameworks (e.g., Arduino-class and microcontroller graphics stacks) that include display drivers for ST7735S.
📐 Compact footprint — 1.8″ diagonal is ideal for handhelds, wearables, and front-panel status displays where space and power are constrained.
🧱 Simple integration — typical pins include VCC, GND, SCL/SCLK, SDA/MOSI, DC (A0), CS, RST, and LED (backlight), allowing a straightforward schematic and PCB routing.
✅ Handheld instruments and meters — small numeric/graphical readouts with simple menus.
✅ Status panels and UI widgets — icons, progress bars, and telemetry dashboards on compact devices.
✅ Learning and demos — perfect for introducing frame buffers, fonts, sprites, and basic graphics pipelines.
✅ Retro/DIY projects — add color output to hobby consoles, synthesizers, or sensor hubs.
✅ Logic/IO levels: the ST7735S controller is commonly used with 3.3 V logic. If your host MCU is 5 V, use proper level shifting or a module explicitly rated for 5 V logic.

✅ SPI wiring: connect SCLK and MOSI (data to display), plus CS, DC (data/command), and RST. Some libraries can share SPI among multiple peripherals; assign unique CS lines and manage bus speed accordingly.
✅ Backlight drive: the LED pin typically powers the backlight. Drive it from a suitable transistor or LED driver rather than a raw MCU pin to manage current and brightness (PWM dimming is common).
✅ Power sequencing: reset the display after power-up and run the recommended init sequence for your library’s ST7735S variant; this sets color mode, orientation, and frame memory access correctly.
✅ Orientation and windowing: use MADCTL (memory access control) to set rotation and RGB/BGR order; use column/row address set commands to define drawing windows for partial updates.
✅ Throughput expectations: SPI is efficient for small UIs and partial redraws; for smooth animation, keep frame regions small, cache sprites, and avoid redrawing static background areas each frame.
✅ ESD & cabling: keep ribbon or jumper cables short; route SPI and control lines as a tidy bundle and decouple VCC near the module with local capacitors.
✅ Mechanical fit: verify bezel/window cutout, standoff locations, and flex clearance in your enclosure; avoid compressing the display stack or the flex tail.
🎨 16-bit RGB 565 is the most common runtime mode, balancing color fidelity and bandwidth.
🌈 18-bit (262K) addressing is supported by the controller; use it when your library and bandwidth allow.
🧮 Address window (partial update): set column and row ranges, then stream pixel data; this enables fast redraws for gauges, icons, or text regions without touching the whole frame.
🔁 Display inversion & gamma: many libraries expose commands to toggle inversion and select gamma curves; tune these for your ambient lighting and contrast preferences.
Pin names you will typically see
LED (backlight anode; sometimes “BL” or “LEDK/LEDA” in paired pins)
Exact pin order and labels can vary between module vendors. Always match your specific board’s silkscreen or datasheet.

🧰 Driver families typically include ST7735/ST7735S support out-of-the-box, providing functions for initialization, setting rotation, writing pixels/rectangles, drawing primitives (lines, circles), text rendering with fonts, and image blitting from RAM or flash.
⚙️ Performance tips: enable SPI burst writes, use DMA (where available), and batch pixels in contiguous windows to minimize command overhead.
🔒 Avoid overdriving pins — do not connect 5 V logic directly unless the module explicitly supports it.
🌡️ Ambient considerations — like most small TFTs, performance and color shift depend on temperature and viewing angle; design your UI with good contrast and font sizes.
🧼 Clean assembly — do not press on the active area; handle by the edges. Keep adhesives and solvents away from the viewing window.
🔆 Backlight lifetime — treat the backlight as a consumable LED string; lower brightness extends life.

blocks.text: Knife Tip T12-XS-K RELIFE For Station

The T12-XS-K is a knife-profile soldering tip from RELIFE designed for use with a compatible soldering station. The K-style edge makes it a versatile everyday tool: you can drag-solder fine-pitch ICs, wick and reflow bridges, tin wires, lift pads gently during rework, and run long seams on connectors and shields—all with one tip by simply changing the angle you present to the joint.
✅ One tip, many jobs — the knife edge can act like a fine point, a small chisel, or a mini spreader depending on the angle.
🎯 Drag-solder control — the edge carries a small bead of solder along QFP/QFN leads for fast, consistent results.
🧼 Bridge cleanup — slide the edge across pins with wick/flux to clear solder bridges neatly.
🔧 Pad work — lift or re-tack small pads and jumpers with better visibility than a conical tip.
🔗 Wire & shield seams — run the flat along connector shells and braid for smooth tinning.
🧩 T12 family geometry — recognizable XS-K knife shape for users who standardize their bench on K-style tips.
✅ Fine-pitch IC assembly — drag-soldering 0.5–0.8 mm lead pitch with flux assist.
✅ Rework & repair — cleaning bridges, re-tinning connectors, pad touch-ups.
✅ Wires & jumpers — fast tinning and tack-soldering of small leads.
✅ Shield cans & ground tabs — controlled heat delivery along edges.
✅ Angle = function — use the very corner for pinpoint joints; roll slightly to use the flat for wicking or seam work.
✅ Flux is your friend — pre-flux pads/pins to improve wetting and reduce required dwell time.
✅ Drag-soldering — pre-load a small bead on the edge, touch the lead row, and pull in one smooth motion.
✅ Bridge removal — lay braid on the bridge, set the knife flat, heat briefly, lift straight up.
✅ Pad lift prevention — keep dwell short; if a joint resists, add flux and re-approach rather than pushing harder.
✅ Tip care — keep a thin tin layer on the edge; clean with brass wool rather than a wet sponge to minimize thermal shock.
🧯 Temperature discipline — use the lowest temperature that achieves quick wetting; avoid extended idle at peak heat.
🧼 Between joints — wipe lightly in brass wool and re-tin; a shiny film protects the edge.
🔍 Inspect often — oxidation shows as dull/dry appearance; re-tin with fresh solder ASAP.
🔒 Storage — always leave the tip tinned when parking or powering down.
🧪 Consumable — tips are wear items; replace when the edge rounds off or plating is compromised.

desc: Raspberry Pi Compute Module 3+ 32GB with BCM2837B0 1.2 GHz, 1 GB LPDDR2, 32 GB eMMC—DDR2-SODIMM form factor for custom carrier boards. وحدة Raspberry Pi Compute Module 3+ بسعة 32GB بمعالج BCM2837B0 بسرعة 1.2 GHz وذاكرة 1 GB eMMC 32 GB—عامل شكل DDR2-SODIMM للوحات الحاملة المخصّصة.

blocks.text: Raspberry Pi Compute Module 3+ 32GB — DDR2-SODIMM SoM for Embedded Designs

The Raspberry Pi Compute Module 3+ 32GB (CM3+/32GB) brings the power of a Pi 3 Model B+ to a compact DDR2-SODIMM system-on-module. It integrates a Broadcom BCM2837B0 (Arm Cortex-A53) @ 1.2 GHz, 1 GB LPDDR2, and 32 GB eMMC—ideal when you need reliable onboard storage and a production-ready footprint for custom carrier boards and industrial designs.
Compute Module 3+ (CM3+/32GB) with 32 GB eMMC, 1 GB LPDDR2, BCM2837B0 @ 1.2 GHz.
Requires a carrier/baseboard with a 200-pin DDR2-SODIMM socket (e.g., Compute Module IO boards or your custom PCB).
🧠 Quad-core 64-bit CPU: BCM2837B0 Cortex-A53 @ 1.2 GHz (Pi 3B+ class).
💾 On-module storage: 32 GB eMMC directly on the primary SD/eMMC interface for robust boot.
🧮 1 GB LPDDR2: ample memory for Linux, graphics, and middleware.
🧩 Full I/O on edge connector: HDMI, USB 2.0 OTG/host, dual CSI/DSI, GPIO, I²C, SPI, UART, SD/SDIO, DPI.
🔌 Standard 200-pin DDR2-SODIMM form factor for low-cost sockets and easy integration.

blocks.text: UrsaLeo UrsaCloud UltraLite Development Kit — Google Cloud-Connected IoT Starter

Kick-start cloud IoT quickly with the UrsaLeo UrsaCloud UltraLite Development Kit. Power it up and the included sensor board streams environmental and motion telemetry to Google Cloud, where you can visualize, store, and process data in the UrsaLeo console, leverage tools like BigQuery, and set event-based alerts—all without building cloud plumbing from scratch. The kit centers on an NXP i.MX6 UltraLite host, plus Thunderboard Sense 2 and a Murata Wi-Fi/BLE board, with a portable router preconfigured for hassle-free connectivity.

blocks.text: Arduino Portenta Cat.M1/NB IoT GNSS Shield — Cellular + GNSS, Nano-SIM, u.FL

Bring low-power cellular and precise positioning to your projects with the Arduino Portenta Cat.M1/NB IoT GNSS Shield. Built around the Thales Cinterion TX62 module, it adds LTE Cat-M1 / NB-IoT connectivity and multi-GNSS (GPS/GLONASS/Galileo/BeiDou) to Portenta and MKR boards—ideal for remote telemetry, asset tracking, and smart-city sensors. GNSS and cellular use dedicated micro u.FL antenna ports; GNSS requires an active antenna.

📶 Dual 3GPP LPWAN: LTE Cat-M1 / NB-IoT (NB1/NB2) with embedded IPv4/IPv6 stack and secure TLS/DTLS clients (HTTP/MQTT/FTP).
🛰️ Multi-GNSS positioning: GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou via u.FL port (3.0 V bias for active antennas).
🔒 Secure & managed: Secure boot, SMS (PDU/Text), AT command control, RGB status LED.
🧰 Portenta/MKR ready: High-density connectors; MKR support with headers. (Not compatible with Portenta Vision Shield at the same time).

blocks.text: Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 IO Board — Dual HDMI 2.0, PCIe x1, USB Hub, RTC

The Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 IO Board is the official reference baseboard that exposes almost every interface of a Compute Module 4 in a bench-friendly form. You get dual full-size HDMI 2.0, PCIe Gen2 x1 for add-in cards, a USB 2.0 hub with internal headers, Gigabit Ethernet with PoE support via HAT, dual DSI & dual CSI connectors, a 40-pin HAT header, and an on-board RTC with battery socket—all powered from a single supply. Ideal for prototyping products, driver bring-up, and lab setups. +1

blocks.text: iCEstick FPGA Evaluation Kit – iCE40HX1K USB Stick Board

The iCEstick FPGA evaluation kit is a USB stick–format board built around the iCE40HX1K device. Plug it into any USB port to prototype HDL designs quickly using the iCE40 toolchain. On-board you get FT2232H USB (for programming + UART), five user LEDs, a Pmod™ 2×6 header, IrDA transceiver, 32 Mbit SPI flash, and a precise 12 MHz MEMS oscillator—all powered over USB. It’s a compact path to learning FPGA flows, testing interfaces, and building small hardware demos at low cost.

blocks.text: ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 N8R2 – Dual USB-C Wi-Fi + BLE Development Board

The ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 N8R2 pairs the ESP32-S3 dual-core LX7 MCU with 8 MB QSPI Flash + 2 MB QSPI PSRAM, giving you enough headroom for advanced Wi-Fi/BLE projects, UI work, and ML/DSP sketches. The board exposes two independent USB functions—a classic USB-to-UART bridge and the SoC’s native USB 2.0 FS (USB-Serial-JTAG/OTG)—so you can power, flash, debug, and even make USB devices with a single cable. Most GPIOs are broken out on breadboard-friendly headers, with Boot/Reset buttons and a built-in RGB LED (GPIO48) for status.

This universal fast adhesive is a clear, colorless ethyl-2-cyanoacrylate formulated for high-speed assembly and field repairs. It delivers reliable bonds on plastics, rubbers, woods, and metals—often fixturing in seconds—and ships in a compact 20 g tube for precise, low-waste application. blocks.text: MAX30102 Heart Rate Sensor – Pulse Oximeter Module (Purple PCB)

Build reliable PPG projects faster with the MAX30102 heart rate sensor—an all-in-one pulse-oximetry front end that integrates red (≈660 nm) + IR (≈880 nm) LEDs, photodiode, low-noise AFE, and an I²C digital interface. A built-in 32-sample FIFO smooths reads, while adjustable LED current (0–50 mA) and pulse width (69–411 µs) help you balance signal quality vs. power. Programmable output rates from 50 to 3200 samples/s give you headroom from low-power wearables to lab demos.
MAX30102 pulse-oximetry / heart-rate sensor module (Purple PCB) × 1
Integrated PPG engine: red + IR emitters, photodiode, AFE, ADC, and ambient-light cancellation (ALC). ALC rejects up to 200 µA of ambient current for cleaner signals.
I²C control + interrupt: standard I²C with INT pin for efficient reads; default slave ID 0b1010111 (0x57).
On-board FIFO: 32-deep buffer reduces MCU servicing overhead during continuous sampling.
Tunable performance: 0–50 mA LED current and 69–411 µs pulse widths for HR/SpO₂ optimization.
Flexible data rates: 50–3200 sps output data rate via registers.
Die temperature readout: on-chip sensor with 0.0625 °C resolution for compensation.

blocks.text: Arduino Mega 2560 R3 CH340G (Board Only — No USB Cable, No Case)

The Arduino Mega 2560 R3 CH340G is a cost-effective, fully compatible Mega-class development board based on the ATmega2560 MCU, fitted with the CH340G USB-to-serial interface for upload and serial monitoring. It keeps the hallmark Mega features—54 digital I/O pins (15 PWM), 16 analog inputs, 4 hardware UARTs, and 16 MHz clock—giving your robotics, CNC/3D-printing, and multi-sensor projects ample I/O and memory headroom. Specs like the operating voltage (5 V), recommended input (7–12 V), and PCB footprint are identical to the reference design, ensuring broad shield compatibility and predictable power behavior .
🔌 CH340G USB interface: Reliable upload/serial without the cost premium of 16U2; widely supported drivers on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
🧲 Board-only listing: No USB cable, no acrylic case/chassis—ideal for integrators who already have accessories (as you requested).
🧩 Drop-in Mega experience: Same pinout, shield geometry, and headers as the reference, so your existing sketches and shields just work .
⚙️ I/O for complex builds: 54 digital I/O with 15 PWM, 16 analog, 4 UARTs, SPI, I²C/TWI, and ICSP—room to grow for motion control and multi-sensor hubs .
🔋 Flexible power: USB, DC jack, or VIN; recommended 7–12 V, absolute 6–20 V, with on-board 5 V and 3.3 V regulators (3.3 V @ 50 mA) .
🛡️ Reference-grade layout: Physical size ≈ 101.52 × 53.3 mm and shield compatibility per R3 notes; auto-reset via DTR capacitor for seamless uploads .
🤖 Multi-axis robots & 3D printers needing many I/O lines
🧪 Data-logging hubs with dozens of sensors/actuators
📟 Education: serial/I²C/SPI labs demonstrating multiple UARTs
🔸 54 digital I/O (D0–D53), 15 PWM on D2–D13 & D44–D46 .
🔹 16 analog inputs (A0–A15) with 10-bit ADC; AREF for external reference .
🟢 I²C/TWI: SDA/SCL on D20/D21; SPI: 50–53 and ICSP header .
🟡 Power header: VIN, 5V, 3V3, GND, IOREF with recommended ranges and cautions .
🔋 Prefer 7–12 V on DC jack or VIN for cooler regulators; below 7 V the 5 V rail may droop; above 12 V regulators overheat—limits 6–20 V .
🪫 Don’t back-feed 5V pin from external supplies unless you know the risks; it bypasses regulation .
🧯 USB protected by resettable polyfuse (extra layer against shorts) .
🔁 Functionally identical in sketches and serial monitor use; difference is only the USB-serial bridge IC.
🧩 Drivers: CH340G uses WCH driver packages; widely available.
💡 Bootload & auto-reset: Behavior remains the same (DTR-to-RESET through 100 nF cap) per R3 design concept .

blocks.text: Analog TDS Sensor Module V1.0 (Gravity-style) — Waterproof Probe, 5V, Analog Output

Meet the Analog TDS Sensor Module V1.0—a compact, stable, and calibration-friendly board for measuring Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) and electrical conductivity (EC) of water. This version pairs a waterproof probe with a precision signal-conditioning board that uses a low-noise op-amp and an onboard oscillator to drive the sensing electrodes with an AC-like excitation—reducing electrode polarization and extending probe life. Read the analog voltage (AO) with your MCU, map it to ppm TDS or mS/cm EC, and you’re ready to monitor RO/DI systems, aquariums, hydroponics, or lab samples.
🔌 Simple 3-wire host interface: VCC, GND, AO to any 5V microcontroller (Arduino, ESP32 5V-tolerant via divider, etc.).
📈 Linear, low-noise output: Precision conditioning around a LMV324-class op-amp for stable readings with averaging.
🔄 AC excitation driver: CD4060-class oscillator helps minimize electrode polarization and measurement drift.
💧 Waterproof probe: Durable stainless electrodes with long lead for immersion measurements.
🎛️ Trim for range: Onboard trimmer (where present) to fine-tune scaling for your container and target ppm.
🧪 Calibratable to ppm or EC: Quick 1- or 2-point calibration using standard solutions (e.g., 1413 μS/cm).
🧰 Compact PCB: About 42 × 32 mm with four M3 mounting holes; JST-style headers for neat wiring.
🧲 Reverse-polarity hints & silkscreen: Clear “A + –” marking near the host header, probe header keyed.
🐠 Aquarium & reef monitoring (ATO/RODI quality, dosing checks)
🥬 Hydroponics nutrient tracking alongside pH & temperature
🚰 RO/DI output quality verification (e.g., alarm when TDS rises)
⚡ Excitation: The board drives the probe with a low-amplitude AC-like signal derived from a CD4060 oscillator stage.
🌀 Sensing: Conductivity of the solution changes the probe impedance; the analog front-end (LMV324 op-amp family) converts it to a voltage.
📊 Reading: Your controller samples AO and converts it to EC (μS/cm) and then TDS (ppm) using a temperature-compensated formula and your calibration constants.
🔌 Connectors: Right 3-pin host header marked A + –; left JST for probe (waterproof).
🖤 Finish: Black PCB, white silkscreen “TDS Meter V1.0”.

blocks.text: Water Turbidity Sensor Module (Probe + Signal Board, 5V, Analog & Digital Output)

Meet the Water Turbidity Sensor Module—a compact, plug-and-play kit that combines an infrared optical probe with a conditioning board to read the clarity of water in real time. Designed around an IR emitter and a matched phototransistor, the sensor measures the light scattered by suspended particles and converts it to a clean voltage level your controller can understand. Whether you’re tracking filter performance, automating aquarium maintenance, logging environmental data, or building a classroom experiment, this module delivers repeatable results with minimal setup.
🔌 Drop-in wiring: 3-wire probe into the board; board provides VCC, GND, AO (analog), DO (digital) to your microcontroller.
⚙️ Two outputs: Read fine-grained analog voltage for calibration or use digital threshold via an onboard comparator (potentiometer adjustable).
🧪 Reliable optical design: IR LED (emitter) + phototransistor geometry reduces color sensitivity and ambient-light effects for stable readings.
🧩 Broad compatibility: Works with Arduino, ESP32/ESP8266, STM32, Raspberry Pi (via ADC), PLCs with 0–5 V inputs, and common data loggers.
💧 Ready for real water: Encapsulated probe head tolerates continuous contact with water; ideal for aquariums, hydroponics, RO/DI monitoring, and lab demos.
🔧 Onboard trim: Set the turbidity trip point for the digital output using the multi-turn potentiometer; onboard LED indicates state at a glance.
📊 Calibratable response: Map voltage to NTU using your own clear/standard samples for best accuracy (application note below).
🧠 Noise-reduced signal chain: Low-ripple 5 V operation and analog filtering provide stable readings even with long sample tubes.
🧴 Compact probe: Round housing with bayonet-style collar makes panel mounting straightforward; see mechanical drawing below.
🧷 Fail-safe wiring labels: Probe pins are molded and labeled VCC / TR / IR on the head for easy verification during assembly.
🧊 Optical turbidity probe (blue collar, translucent head)
🟦 Signal conditioning module (AO/DO outputs, trim pot, indicator LED)
🪢 3-core lead between probe and board (assumption: 20–30 cm; confirm as needed)
✨ IR emission: The IR LED sends light through the water sample.
🛰️ Scatter collection: Suspended particles scatter light toward the phototransistor.
🔄 Proportional signal: More particles → more scatter → higher sensor current → a higher AO voltage (after conditioning).
🚦 Thresholding: The onboard comparator compares AO to your setpoint to drive DO high/low for simple on/off logic and alarms.
🐠 Aquariums & aquatic farms: filter clogging detection, water change timing
🥬 Hydroponics & nutrient tanks: clarity tracking after dosing
🧪 Education & STEM labs: optics, scattering, environmental science
🏭 Process water checks & coolant systems (non-hazardous fluids)
🌿 Environmental sampling (rivers, ponds) with portable data loggers
🧲 Mounting: Round body with locking blue collar; suitable for panel/snap fit (confirm your preferred method)
🧾 Internal layout: Left cavity = IR Emitting Diode; right cavity = TR (Photo-Transistor). Connector at base labeled VCC / TR / IR for the head.
📈 Analog output (AO): ~0.2–4.5 V proportional to turbidity
🎚️ Digital output (DO): TTL-level, active on threshold; adjustable via potentiometer
🎯 Recommended turbidity range: 0–1000 NTU usable; 0–3000 NTU extended with custom calibration (assumption; set by application)
🔁 Repeatability: good with stable temperature and supply; use averaging for best results
🚿 Fluid compatibility: Freshwater; non-corrosive, non-solvent liquids. Avoid hot, viscous, or solvent media.
🟥 VCC — 5 V to IR LED and board bias
🟡 TR — Phototransistor sense to conditioning circuit
🟦 IR — IR LED cathode/anode lead (as wired on board)
🟣 DO — Digital threshold (to MCU GPIO / interrupt)
🔌 Power the Water Turbidity Sensor Module at 5 V.
🟢 Connect AO to an analog pin (A0).
🟣 Optionally connect DO to a digital pin (D2) for alarm/threshold.
🎚️ Place the probe into your water sample; wait 3–5 s for stabilization.
🧭 Turn the potentiometer until the onboard LED toggles at your desired clarity.
📊 Read AO values, average (e.g., 10–50 samples), and map to NTU using your calibration curve.
🌫️ Reference points: Use clear water (0 NTU proxy) and a known turbidity standard (e.g., 100–500 NTU for your range).
📐 Curve fitting: Record AO for each reference; fit a 2-point linear or polynomial curve to convert AO→NTU.
🔁 Stability: Keep temperature, container geometry, and immersion depth consistent between measurements.
🧼 Maintenance: Rinse after each use; avoid fingerprints or film on the optical windows.
🚫 Not for hot liquids, solvents, or strong acids/alkalis.
🧯 Observe correct polarity; reverse connection may damage the IR LED.
🧽 Keep the optical windows clean; deposits cause drift.
🧊 Store dry and dust-free when not in use.

The IC 7486 (74HC86N) is a quad 2-input Exclusive-OR (XOR) logic gate in a DIP-14 package. Each IC contains four independent XOR gates that output HIGH when the number of HIGH inputs is odd. Belonging to the high-speed CMOS 74HC logic family, this chip is widely used in digital logic design, arithmetic circuits, parity generation, and error detection systems.
DIP-14 package for prototyping and breadboard use.
Low power consumption and high noise immunity.

blocks.text: The IC 7485 is a 4-bit magnitude comparator that outputs logic signals indicating whether input word A is greater than, equal to, or less than input word B. It belongs to the 74HC/74LS logic family and is commonly used in arithmetic logic units (ALUs), digital sorting, and threshold detection systems. Both 74HC85 (CMOS) and 74LS85 (TTL) versions are available, providing compatibility for different design requirements.
4-bit binary comparator with outputs: A>B, A=B, A<B.
Cascade inputs and outputs for multi-stage comparison (8, 12, 16 bits).

blocks.text: IC 74139 – Dual 2-to-4 Line Decoder / Demultiplexer (74HC139 / 74LS139, DIP-16)

blocks.text: The IC 7414 is a hex inverter with Schmitt-trigger inputs, designed for clean signal switching and enhanced noise immunity. Each of the six independent inverters converts a logic signal while filtering out slow or noisy transitions, making it especially useful for debouncing mechanical switches and wave shaping. Available in 74HC14 CMOS (2–6V) and 74LS14 TTL (5V) families, this IC is widely used in timing circuits, oscillators, and digital input conditioning.
Six Schmitt-trigger inverters in a single DIP-14 package.
Hysteresis improves noise immunity and ensures clean transitions.
Ideal for debouncing buttons, wave shaping, and square-wave generation.

blocks.text: The NodeMCU V3 ESP8266 development board is a versatile module tailored for IoT and embedded projects. It integrates a CH340 USB-to-serial converter via a Type-C connector, making it easy to program and power using modern USB ports. Based on the ESP8266 (ESP-12E module), it supports Wi-Fi connectivity, GPIOs, ADC, PWM, I²C, and more. The board is compatible with Arduino IDE and Lua/NodeMCU firmware.

This relay can be used to switch High power (whether AC or DC) to a load by driving the relay coil with a far much lower voltage and current. When Current flows through the relay coil, It makes or breaks its contacts through electromagnetic induction. A relay contacts comprises of the Normally-Open (NO) and Normally Closed (NC) contacts. These refer to the state of the relay contacts when the relay coil is not energized. When driving a relay coil from a digital output or transistor, always connect a diode in reverse bias across the coil of the relay in other to avoid the resulting back-emf that appears across the coil of the relay when its turned off from damaging the digital device or transistor.

blocks.text: TEMT6000 Ambient Light Sensor Module – Analog Output for Light Intensity Measurement
TEMT6000 Ambient Light Sensor Module – Analog Output for Light Intensity Measurement

The TEMT6000 Ambient Light Sensor Module is a compact, high-sensitivity light sensor designed to provide precise ambient light measurements for a wide range of electronic applications. This sensor mimics the human eye’s response to light, making it ideal for projects that require automatic brightness adjustment, smart lighting, and energy-saving solutions.
With its analog output, the TEMT6000 delivers real-time light intensity readings, allowing your microcontroller or development board to react to changing light conditions with exceptional accuracy.
Analog output for easy microcontroller integration
Spectral response similar to the human eye
Compact size, ideal for portable or space-constrained applications
Suitable for indoor and outdoor light monitoring

This sensor module utilizes a phototransistor (TEMT6000) to provide an analog voltage output proportional to the light intensity in the environment. The spectral response closely follows that of the human eye, making it highly suitable for applications requiring light detection that mimics human perception.
The TEMT6000 is especially advantageous for daylight sensing, enabling systems to adjust illumination levels or display brightness based on surrounding light conditions.
Unlike digital light sensors, the analog output of the TEMT6000 allows for continuous, real-time readings with fine resolution, making it ideal for precise light measurement tasks.

1. PCB Manufacturing: This solder mask is used during the fabrication of printed circuit boards. After the PCB has been etched and copper traces applied, the solder mask is applied to cover the areas where solder is not needed.

2. Soldering Process: During the assembly of electronic components onto the PCB, the solder mask serves as a protective layer, preventing solder from flowing onto unwanted areas of the board and causing short circuits or other electrical issues.

3. UV Curing: The UV aspect of this solder mask means that it requires exposure to ultraviolet light to cure or harden. Once applied to the PCB, the solder mask is exposed to UV light in a controlled environment to initiate the curing process.

4. Insulation and Protection: Once cured, the solder mask provides insulation and protection to the copper traces on the PCB, shielding them from moisture, dust, and other contaminants that could potentially lead to electrical failures or corrosion over time.

blocks.text: ADS1118 16-Bit I2C 16 AD Converter ADC SPI Communication Module

In this article, we are interfacing an ADS1118 16-bit ADC module with an Arduino. An analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is a device that converts an analog signal, such as the voltage output of a sensor, into a digital representation that a microcontroller can understand and process. An ADC can be used to read and process analog signals on the Arduino, which is a microcontroller.

There are several ADCs available for use with the Arduino, ranging from simple, low-resolution converters to high-precision, high-resolution devices. For this project, we are using ADS1118 16-Bit ADC.
There are just a few basic steps, and no additional hardware is needed for the interface. As a result, the code is simpler to comprehend. Let’s dive in right now and find out more!

The ADS1118 is a precise, low-power, 16-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC). The ADS1118 combines a PGA, voltage reference, oscillator, and temperature sensor. blocks.text: ADS1115 16-Bit ADC- 4 Channel with Programmable Gain Amplifier

ADS1115 16-Bit ADC – 4 Channel with Programmable Gain Amplifier is mostly used for microcontrollers project which needs an analog-to-digital converter or when you want a higher-precision ADC. ADS1115 16-Bit ADC- provides 16-bit precision at 860 samples/second over I2C. The chip can be configured as 4 single-end input channels or two differential channels.

Additionally, ADC also includes a programmable gain amplifier, up to x16, to help boost up smaller single/differential signals to the full range. We like this ADC because it can run from 2V to 5V power/logic, can measure a large range of signals and it’s super easy to use. It is a great general-purpose 16-bit converter.

The ADS1115 chip is fairly small so it comes on a breakout board with ferrites to keep the AVDD and AGND quiet. Interfacing is done via I2C. The address can be changed to one of four options (see the datasheet table 5) so you can have up to 4 ADS1115’s connect on a single 2-wire I2C bus for 16 single end inputs.

To get you start, we have example code for both the Raspberry Pi (in our Adafruit Pi Python library) and Arduino (in our ADS1X15 Arduino library repository) Simply connect GND to ground, VDD to your logic power supply, and SCL/SDA to your microcontroller’s I2C port and run the example code to start reading data.

blocks.text: Arduino MKR WAN 1310 LoRa Connectivity (Original Made In Italy)
Arduino MKR WAN 1310 allows you to build your next smart project. Ever wanted an automated house? Or a smart garden?

The Arduino MKR WAN 1310 board provides a practical and cost effective solution to add LoRa® connectivity to projects requiring low power. This open source board can be connected to the Arduino IoT Cloud.

The MKR WAN 1310, brings in a series of improvements when compared to its predecessor, the MKR WAN 1300. While still based on the Microchip® SAMD21 low power processor, the Murata CMWX1ZZABZ LoRa® module, and the MKR family’s characteristic crypto chip (the ECC508), the MKR WAN 1310 includes a new battery charger, a 2MByte SPI Flash, and improved control of the board’s power consumption.

The latest modifications have considerably improved the battery life on the MKR WAN 1310. When properly configured, the power consumption is now as low as 104uA! It is also possible to use the USB port to supply power (5V) to the board; run the board with or without batteries – the choice is yours.

Data logging and other OTA (Over The Air) functions are now possible since the inclusion of the on board 2MByte Flash. This new exciting feature will let you transfer configuration files from the infrastructure onto the board, create your own scripting commands, or simply store data locally to send it whenever the connectivity is best. Whilst the MKR WAN 1310’s crypto chip adds further security by storing credentials & certificates in the embedded secure element.
These features make it the perfect IoT node and building block for low-power wide-area IoT devices.

Check the Arduino Forum for questions about the Arduino Language, or how to make your own Projects with Arduino. Need any help with your board please get in touch with the official Arduino User Support as explained in our Contact Us page.
The Arduino MKR WAN 1310 is based on the SAMD21 microcontroller.

If you want to detect methane gases with your projects, you will need sensors. If you need any data on the sensitive material then, the MQ-4 High Sensitivity Gas Methane (CNG) Detector Gas Sensor Module is a quite good solution.

This is a simple to use MQ-4 High Sensitivity Gas Methane (CNG) Detector Sensor Module which can sense the presence of Compressed Natural Gas(CNG), methane(CH4), etc in the air. The module uses our MQ-4 sensor. It simplifies the interface to the odd pin spacing of the sensor and provides the interface through standard 4 x 0.1″ header pins.

It provides an analog output corresponding to the concentration of the gases in the air and an easy-to-use digital output. The onboard potentiometer can be used to set the maximum gas concentration beyond which the digital output gets triggered. The MQ-4 can detect natural gas concentrations anywhere from 200 to 10000ppm.
Just power the module with 5V set the threshold and you can start getting the gas concentration of the air around the sensor! An onboard LED signals the presence of any gas.

The digital output can be easily interfaced with microcontrollers and other circuits. The analog output can be hooked up to an ADC of a microcontroller to get a wide range of sensor readings. This is a simple-to-use compressed natural gas (CNG) sensor, suitable for sensing natural gas (composed of mostly Methane [CH4]) concentrations in the air.

Dual Led 0.28 ” Display for DC0-100V 100A Voltage and Current Test Digital Instrument, Digital Meter Panel Amplifier Red Blue 100A
This is 0.28″ 5 Wires Red Led Digital Dual DC 100V 100A Ammeter Voltmeter. This meter will measure up to 100 VDC with a 0.1-volt resolution.

One thing to note is, this meter has 2 wiring harnesses. One harness is to provide power for the meters, that’s the 2 poles with a RED and a BLACK lead. Small size, portable, the magnitudes of voltage and current are displayed on the same screen at the same time.

This can be supplied anywhere from 6 volts DC up to 30 VDC. This is a separate power supply that is isolated from the source, it is possible to use the same supply but it seems to affect the amp meter reading. The 3 wire harness is used for a ground that connects directly to the battery or supply ground of the load.

Note: There are two different wiring variants (i.e. yellow wire and Green wire ) with the same working functionality is available which will be shipped randomly. Use the following guidelines according to your version.
CASE 1: Onboard Wiring Instructions for “Yellow” Wire connection
1. Thin Red Wire (VCC): positive pole of power supply input (4.5-30V)
(Note: if the measuring signal is less than 30V and the power is adequate, can be the power supply of module)
2. Thin Black Wire (GND): the negative pole of power supply input (4.5-30V, common ground with measuring signal)
3. Green Wire (VIN): positive pole of measuring signal input (0-100V)
4. Thick Red Wire (I ): positive pole of current input (series connect on the power supply cathode)
5. Thick Black Wire (I-): the negative pole of current input (series connect on the power supply cathode)
Note: If the input voltage is more than 5V, then, please use a buck converter.
Note: This Product Does Not include a shunt.
CASE 2: Onboard Wiring Instructions for “Green” Wire connection
(The current range of 10A requires the external shunt connection process)
1. Connect the lines which are not connected well, and do not touch other places.

2. The shunt is connected to the negative pole of the measuring system (the shunt itself does not distinguish the direction, and the connection is fixed to the two large screw holes in the distributor.
3. According to the current direction, the green line ( ) and the black line (-) of the three lines are respectively screwed on the two small screws of the shunt.
4. Connect the red line of the three lines to the positive pole of the measuring system.

5. The power supply line in the two lines is connected to the appropriate power supply (and the voltage between the black lines in the three lines. It is suggested to be connected to the 12V, at the same time, the electric power black lines in the two lines are wrapped with insulating tape, so do not encounter other places, so as not to cause a short circuit).

6. The above 1-5 steps are suitable for the use of common ground; for independent power supply occasions, the red and black lines of power supply in two lines are respectively connected to both sides of the positive and negative poles of the power supply (the power supply voltage <28V, suggested to be about 12V).
It measures up to 100V and 100A DC.
Very handy and small in size.
It requires a power supply of 5V.

desc: DC-DC Boster MT3608 3V~28Vdc Adjustable Step-Up Converter Module 2A Type C USB It’s efficient up to 93% It can source a good amount of current The maximum output current: 2A Input voltage: 2V-24V DC The maximum output voltage: 5V-28V DC

blocks.text: DC-DC Boster MT3608 3V~28Vdc Adjustable Step-Up Converter Module 2A Type C USB
The MT3608 2A Max DC-DC Step Up Power Module Booster Power Module is a low-cost module that can step-up a 2 to 24V input voltage up to a 5 to 28V output at up to 2A.
DC-DC boost converters step up the input voltage to a higher voltage while also stepping down the available current since the module can’t output more power than its inputs.

This boost converter is adjustable and capable of outputting a voltage in the range of 5.0 to 28V at a continuous current of up to 1.5A depending on input/output voltage settings with 1A available with most settings.
Since it is a boost converter, the input voltage must be lower than the output voltage.
The device is able to use low ESR bulk ceramic capacitors rather than electrolytic caps which avoids long-term aging concerns and contributes to the compact packaging.
The MT3608 converter IC has over-current and thermal limiting features built-in to safely shut the device down if driven too hard.
The module has a single-turn potentiometer for adjustment of the output voltage.
Turning the pot CW decreases the output voltage while turning it CCW increases the output voltage.
The upper limit of the adjustment range will depend on the input voltage and the load. With a 9V input for instance, at 1A, the upper voltage limit will be approximately 20V.
These are compact boards with 4 solder pads for making connections.
VOUT- = Ground. Connected to VIN- on the module.
The input voltage should not exceed the maximum input voltage.
Peak current output current is not more than 2A for input & output.
Please be noted that the output voltage should be higher than the input voltage.
It can source a good amount of current.
It is an inexpensive converter module.
It’s simple to adjust to get your desired increase in voltage.

name: Servo Driver Module Shield 16 Channel
desc: Servo Driver Module Shield 16 Channel The I2C input, PWM output control 16 roads, steering gear can 16 roads. The steering gear power independent V + input maximum 6 V. Logic signals and logical power independent output for 3V to 5 V. 40-1000 Hz frequency. Terminal block for power input. Reverse polarity protection on the terminal block input Green power-good LED

blocks.text: You want to make a cool robot, maybe a hexapod walker, or maybe just a piece of art with a lot of moving parts. Or maybe you want to drive a lot of LEDs with precise PWM output. Then you realize that your microcontroller has a limited number of PWM outputs! Here is the Servo Driver Module Shield 16 Channel to help you out!!!
What now? You could give up OR you could just get our handy PWM and Servo driver shield. It’s now Arduino-ready and works with any Arduino that uses shields: Uno, Mega, ADK, it’s all good.
Using only two pins, control 16 free-running PWM outputs! You can even chain up 62 breakouts to control up to 992 PWM outputs

It’s an I2C-controlled PWM driver with a built-in clock. That means that, unlike the TLC5940 family, you do not need to continuously send it the signal to tie up your microcontroller, it’s completely free running!

It is 5V compliant, which means you can control it from a 3.3V microcontroller and still safely drive up to 6V outputs (this is good for when you want to control white or blue LEDs with 3.4+ forward voltages)
6 address select pins so you can wire up to 62 of these on a single i2c bus, a total of 992 outputs – that’s a lot of servos or LEDs
Adjustable frequency PWM up to about 1.6 KHz
12-bit resolution for each output – for servos, that means about 4us resolution at a 60Hz update rate
Configurable push-pull or an open-drain output
The output enable pin to quickly disable all the outputs
We wrapped up this lovely chip into a breakout board with a couple of nice extras
Terminal block for power input (or you can use the 0.1″ breakouts on the side)
Reverse polarity protection on the terminal block input
3 pin connectors in groups of 4 so you can plug in 16 servos at once (Servo plugs are slightly wider than 0.1″ so you can only stack 4 next to each other on 0.1″ header
A spot to place a big capacitor on the V+ line (in case you need it)
330-ohm series resistors on all the output lines to protect them, and to make driving LEDs trivial
Solder jumpers for the 6 address select pins

The MT3608 2A Max DC-DC Step Up Power Module Booster Power Module is a low-cost module that can step-up a 2 to 24V input voltage up to a 5 to 28V output at up to 2A.
DC-DC boost converters step up the input voltage to a higher voltage while also stepping down the available current since the module can’t output more power than its inputs.

This boost converter is adjustable and capable of outputting a voltage in the range of 5.0 to 28V at a continuous current of up to 1.5A depending on input/output voltage settings with 1A available with most settings.
Since it is a boost converter, the input voltage must be lower than the output voltage.
The device is able to use low ESR bulk ceramic capacitors rather than electrolytic caps which avoids long-term aging concerns and contributes to the compact packaging.
The MT3608 converter IC has over-current and thermal limiting features built-in to safely shut the device down if driven too hard.
The module has a single-turn potentiometer for adjustment of the output voltage.
Turning the pot CW decreases the output voltage while turning it CCW increases the output voltage.
The upper limit of the adjustment range will depend on the input voltage and the load. With a 9V input for instance, at 1A, the upper voltage limit will be approximately 20V.
