name: MBR20100CT Dual Schottky Diode 100V 20A

blocks.text: The MBR20100 is a dual Schottky diode with common cathode in a To-220 Package for high current applications. Each diode has a forward current of 10A, hence the IC can push upto 20A through it with a peak reverse voltage of 100V

blocks.v: Anode · Anode of first Schottky Diode
Common Cathode · Cathode of both Schottky Diodes
Anode · Anode of second Schottky Diode

blocks.text: Forward Current: 20A for dual diode at 50% duty cycle
Note: Complete Technical Details can be found at the MBR20100 datasheet given at the end of this page.

The MBR20100 is a rectifier dual diode that is commonly used in Converter circuits. The package consists of two diodes in parallel increasing the current rating and reducing the package size and cost. Since the Schottky diodes are faster and efficient (low voltage drop) they are commonly preferred over normal diodes provided the reverse voltage is need not be high.

Also since the diode package has common cathode it can be used in protection circuits and filter circuits for voltage clamping. So if you are looking for a high current dual Schottky diode then MBR20100 might be the right choice.

Using the MBR20100 is pretty much straight forward; the package has only three pins because the cathode pins are tied together and provided as single output pin as shown in the pinouts image above. The Anode pin of both the diodes are given as pin 1 and Pin 3 which can be combined if the diode has to be used as a single device, else it can also be used as different pins for voltage clamping or Protection circuits.

When the device conducts in forward voltage it can supply upto 20A when both diodes are combined (10A each) with a voltage drop of only 0.8V (per leg) at 125°C. Care should be taken that the diode does not experience high reverse voltage since the Peak reverse breakdown voltage is only 100V. Also the forward voltage drop can be as high as 1V when operating with high forward current, more details can be found at the MBR20100 datasheet linked at the bottom of this page.

blocks.text: 5631BS 3-Digit 7 Segment LED Display – 0.56 inch – Red – Common Anode

The 5631BS is a 3-digit 7-segment LED display module designed for displaying numerical data in compact electronics projects. With its 0.56-inch digit height, it provides excellent readability while maintaining a compact footprint.

This display uses a common anode (CA) configuration, ideal for interfacing with various microcontrollers and display drivers. Each digit contains 7 segments arranged to represent numbers from 0 to 9, with a bright red color emission and black background for high contrast.
Whether you’re designing a digital voltmeter, timer, or embedded control panel, the 5631BS is a dependable and easy-to-use numeric display.

blocks.text: A robust 180 Ω 2W axial resistor for power and general-purpose electronics. Ideal for voltage dividers, pull-ups, current limiting, and signal conditioning where higher dissipation is required.
High power rating 2W: handles elevated dissipation in compact builds.
Stable resistance 180 Ω: consistent performance for precise networks.
Axial leads: easy hand-soldering and breadboard/PCB use.
Wide usability: works in analog, power, and digital support roles.
Clear marking: value code for quick identification.
Use for voltage dividers, reference networks, RC timing, and pull-ups/pull-downs.
Leave airflow space when dissipating near 2 W; avoid enclosing tightly.
For precise ratios, match tolerances across divider resistors.
Pre-form leads gently to fit hole spacing and reduce stress.
Power supply bleeder or discharge networks.
Verify expected power dissipation P = I²R = V²/R stays below 2 W with margin.
Keep parts clear of heat-sensitive materials when running warm.
Do not bend leads right at the body; support the lead before forming.
Observe proper creepage/clearance at higher voltages.
Electrically tested for value and tolerance.
Minor color/mark differences can occur between batches.
Packed to protect leads from deformation during transit.
Q1: Can I use it as a bleeder resistor on a DC bus?** Yes—ensure the dissipation and voltage limits are within safe ratings.
Q2: Is it suitable for precision dividers?** For tighter accuracy, pair with matched-tolerance parts or calibrate in-circuit.
Q3: Can it be used on breadboards?** Yes—axial leads fit breadboards and standard perf/PCBs.
Q4: What wire gauge are the leads?** Standard axial lead size for 2W class; fits common PCB holes.
Q5: Does orientation matter?** No—resistors are non-polarized.

blocks.text: The 5612AS-1-18 360 is a 2-digit 7-segment LED display delivering crisp red numerals at a standard 0.56″ (≈14.2 mm) digit height. It comes in an 18-pin (9×2) THT package with Common Cathode architecture per digit—pin 14 = DIG1 (cathode), pin 13 = DIG2 (cathode)—as per the provided CC pinout. The compact 25.0 × 19.0 × 8.0 mm body and 2.54 mm pitch make it breadboard- and panel-friendly for counters, meters, clocks, and embedded HMI.
✅ True CC topology: separate cathode per digit (13, 14) simplifies multiplexing with common high-side sources.
🔴 High-contrast red segments: clear visibility on a dark face; ideal under normal indoor lighting.
📐 Standard 0.56″ height: readable at a glance, fits common bezels and panels.
🧩 18-pin 9×2, 2.54 mm pitch: robust THT leads for fast prototyping and solid production soldering.
⚙️ MCU-ready: works with Arduino/AVR/ESP/STM32/PIC and drivers like ULN2803A (segment sinks) + PNP/P-MOS for digit sources, or CC drivers (e.g., MAX7219).
🔒 Reliable build: molded top, beveled segments, decimal point on each digit.
Outline matches drawing: 25 mm length, 19 mm width, 8 mm height.
9×2 pin grid, 2.54 mm pitch; through-hole mounting.
10 A₂, 11 B₂, 12 C₂, 13 DIG2 (Cathode), 14 DIG1 (Cathode), 15 D₁, 16 E₁, 17 F₁, 18 DP₁
1 E₂, 2 D₂, 3 C₁, 4 B₁, 5 A₁, 6 G₂, 7 F₂, 8 G₁, 9 DP₂

⚡ Driving rule: For CC, segments light when their pins are driven HIGH while the active digit cathode (13 or 14) is held LOW. In multiplex, alternate digits at 1–2 kHz and size resistors for peak current.
🧮 Resistor estimate: R ≈ (Vcc − Vf − Vdriver)/Iseg. Example 5 V, Vf=2.0 V, I=10 mA → ≈300 Ω → use 330 Ω E12.
📦 Discrete approach: MCU GPIO → resistors → segment pins; ULN2803A sinks segments; PNP/P-MOS sources digit commons.
🧠 Driver IC: MAX7219 natively supports CC multi-digit LED—maps easily with 2 unused digits (or chain devices).
🔁 Flicker-free: keep per-digit refresh ≥1 kHz; consider 5–10 mA average per segment for long life.

blocks.text: The BC547 is a versatile NPN bipolar junction transistor (BJT) housed in a compact TO-92 package. Designed for low-power amplification and switching, this transistor is popular for general-purpose audio, signal and control applications. With a collector-emitter breakdown voltage of 45 V and continuous collector current up to 100 mA, the BC547 provides plenty of headroom for interfacing logic circuits, driving small loads and building analog amplifiers. Its high DC current gain (hFE) classification ranges from 110 to 800 across A/B/C variants, and the device exhibits very low saturation voltage and low noise for clean signal amplification. Thanks to a typical transition frequency around 300 MHz and operation up to +150 °C, the BC547 is suitable for both hobbyist projects and professional designs.
• Voltage & current capability: collector–emitter voltage (VCEO) 45 V, collector–base voltage 50 V, emitter–base voltage 6 V; collector current up to 100 mA and power dissipation 500 mW.
• High gain classifications: hFE ranges from 110–220 (A class) through 200–450 (B) to 420–800 (C).
• Low saturation voltage: VCE(sat) ≈ 90 mV at 10 mA base current; < 0.2 V at 100 mA collector current.
• Fast switching: transition frequency (~300 MHz) supports high-frequency operation.
• Low noise: noise figure ≈ 2 dB for use in audio pre-amplifiers.
• Package: TO-92 with 3 terminals – 1: Collector, 2: Base, 3: Emitter.
• Signal amplification: pre-amplifiers, oscillators and linear amplifier stages.
• Switching: LED drivers, relay drivers and TTL interface circuits.
• Audio circuits: low-noise stages in audio pre-amps.
• General purpose: analog/digital interfacing, sensor signal conditioning, hobbyist and educational projects.

blocks.text: MFRC522 RFID Module 13.56MHz Reader/Writer + Card & Tag (SPI)

Meet the MFRC522 RFID Module—a compact, 13.56 MHz reader/writer board for ISO/IEC 14443A tags (MIFARE® Classic/NTAG). It’s the classic “RC522” board used in countless Arduino and ESP projects. Designed around NXP’s MFRC522 IC, the module communicates via SPI (up to 10 Mbit/s) at 3.3 V logic. Typical read distance is 0–50 mm with the bundled S50‑class media. blocks.text: Water Level Detection Sensor Module — Analog Output, 3–5V, 40×16 mm Detection Area

This water level detection sensor is a low‑cost, resistive probe board that outputs an analog voltage proportional to the wet length of its exposed traces. It’s ideal for quick experiments with Arduino/ESP32/Raspberry Pi to detect presence, drops, leaks, or approximate level within a short range. The sensing area is approximately 40 × 16 mm, and the module operates from 3–5 V, drawing less than 20 mA.

Unlike float switches or ultrasonic sensors, this board is designed for near‑surface/short‑range detection. For continuous immersion or corrosive liquids, consider a sealed or non‑contact solution; this board is best for learning, prototyping, and indicative sensing.
Operating voltage: 3–5 V DC (5 V nominal)

Quick start: Connect +5 V → +V, GND → GND, A0 → SIG. Read the analog value; higher values correspond to more wet area. Calibrate thresholds for your use case.
Resistive principle: Water bridging across adjacent exposed traces forms a resistance ladder. The board converts this to a proportional output voltage.
Calibration: Map the dry reading and the fully‑wet reading to your 0–100% scale. Use moving average or median filter to reduce noise.
Corrosion & lifespan: The exposed copper can corrode with long‑term exposure, electrolytic action, or contaminated water. For reliability:
Use distilled water for tests where possible.
Power‑gate the sensor and sample intermittently (e.g., MOSFET on +V) to reduce electrolysis.
Consider anti‑corrosion or float/ultrasonic level sensors for permanent installations.
Not a linear level gauge: Output is monotonic but not perfectly linear; treat readings as indicative.
EMI/ESD: Keep leads short; add a 100 nF ceramic decoupling near +V.

Example thresholding: For leak detection, trigger alarm if averaged reading rises above a dry baseline + margin. For simple tank “near full” indication, mount the board vertically and set a threshold near the desired waterline.

blocks.text: This 13V 0.5W Zener diode (axial DO‑35/DO‑204AH package) provides a stable reference around 13.0 V for regulation, clamping and over‑voltage protection. The device targets the popular 500 mW small‑signal Zener class (BZX55/BZX79/ZPD families). Nominal Zener voltage is specified at a test current of 5 mA, with ±5% tolerance (typical “C‑tolerance” range). It’s a simple, reliable building block for power rails, ADC references, and snubbers.

Why this value? Around 13 V the Zener exhibits a positive temperature coefficient typical of mid‑range voltages, making it suitable for general clamp/reference tasks while keeping dynamic impedance reasonably low.

blocks.text: DC-DC Step-Up (Boost) Converter Module — XL6009E1, 400kHz, up to 35V, up to 4A

If you need a compact XL6009E1 boost converter to raise a DC input to a higher regulated output, this module is the proven workhorse. It uses the genuine XL6009E1 controller at 400kHz with an integrated high-current switch, giving fast transient response and strong efficiency in a small footprint. Dial the multi‑turn trim pot to any target voltage within the supported range, and the board will hold regulation across varying loads when properly heatsunk and within limits.

Highlights at a glance: adjustable 5–35V output (module), typical up to 94% efficiency (load/conditions dependent), and up to 4A peak output capability (see notes). The onboard controller supports a wide input range at the IC level and exposes an EN pin internally; the module breaks out simple I/O pads for quick wiring.

🔎 Why this module? Compared with older 52kHz designs, the 400kHz XL6009E1 allows smaller inductors and capacitors, reducing ripple and board size. It also includes soft‑start, current limit, and thermal protection inside the chip.

blocks.text: The STMicroelectronics NE555N timer IC is the classic single timer/oscillator in a DIP‑8 package. It supports monostable and astable operation, delivering precise timing from microseconds to hours via an external R/C network. Its push‑pull output is TTL‑compatible at 5 V and can sink/source substantial current for small loads (LEDs, buzzers, logic inputs) and, via a transistor, relays and motors.

Engineers and makers rely on the 555 for rapid prototyping and robust designs thanks to its simplicity, wide supply range, and abundant reference circuits. This listing targets STMicroelectronics NE555N (DIP‑8); always consult the datasheet for exact electrical limits.

blocks.text: PIC16F676 is a microcontroller good for learning and experimenting for engineers because it has high flash memory rewrite cycle. The controller has 2KBytes flash memory which is enough for starters to develop basic programs. Also the 12 GPIO are designed for handling 20mA current (LED driving capability) by which beginners can connect peripheral at hand with less caution.

PIC16F676 has very few features and it cannot be used for developing advanced applications. It is used for developing small applications (like display driver) and for developing programs by beginners who want to enter microcontroller platform.
Any microcontroller is needed to be programmed before installing in any system or application. So first we need to program the controller PIC16F676.
Entire process of programming PIC16F676 goes like this:
First list all the functions to be executed by this controller.
Next write these functions in ‘IDE software’ using ‘C’ language.
This IDE software can be downloaded for free on company website.
After writing the desired program compile it for error elimination.
For a successful compilation IDE application generates HEX file for the written program.
Choose the programming device (usually ‘PIC kit 3’ or ‘PIC kit 2’) which establishes communication between PC and PIC16F676.
Connect the programming device to microcontroller appropriately.
Run the HEX file dumping software which is related to the chosen programming device.
Choose the appropriate program HEX file and burn this HEX file in PIC16F676 flash memory.
Disconnect the programmer and connect the appropriate peripherals for the controller.
After connecting the power, the controller executes this HEX code saved in the memory (which is written program) and creates response as instructed.

name: 74154 4-Line to 16-Line Decoder/Demultiplexer IC
desc: IC Name: 74HC148 Package/Case: DIP-16

blocks.text: Each or these 4-line-to-16-line decoders utilizes TTL circuitry to decode four binary-coded inputs into one of sixteen mutually exclusive outputs when both the strobe inputs, G1 and G2, are low. The demultiplexing function is performed by using the 4 input lines to address the output line, passing data from one of the strobe inputs with the other strobe input low. When either strobe input is high, all outputs are high. These demultiplexers are ideally suited for implementing high-performance memory decoders. All inputs are buffered and input clamping diodes are provided to minimize transmission-line effects and thereby simplify system design.
1. Decodes 4 binary-coded inputs into one of 16 mutually exclusive outputs
2. Performs the demultiplexing function by distributing data from one input line to any one of 16 outputs
3. Input clamping diodes simplify system design

blocks.text: One of the main drawback of TTL ICs are, output voltage will be in the range of 5 volts. So the outputs of these ICs cannot be used to drive high current loads such as lamps or relays. 7407 ICs are normally used in such situations. These devices perform the boolean function Y = A in positive logic, which means if the input is at logical HIGH, output will be at logical HIGH. Similarly, if the input is at logical LOW, output will be at logical LOW. But the magnitude of input and output voltage will be different. Input voltage will be 5.5V. But the output voltage will be 30V. Pinout diagram of 7407 IC is given below.

name: CD4075 IC Three OR Gates 3-input

blocks.text: CD4075 – An IC with Three OR Gates (3-input)
The CD4075 is a CMOS chip with three 3-input OR gates. Because each gate has three inputs and it has three gates inside, it’s usually called a Triple 3-Input OR Gate.
An OR gate is a logic gate that outputs HIGH if either of its inputs is HIGH. Each of the OR-gates in this chip has 3 inputs.

blocks.v: 1, 3, 13 · Input · Inputs A of the three OR gates
2, 4, 12 · Input · Inputs B of the three OR gates
5, 8, 11 · Input · Inputs C of the three OR gates
6, 9, 10 · Output · Outputs from the three OR gates

blocks.text: A 3-input OR gate works just like a normal OR gate. Its output becomes HIGH if any of the inputs are HIGH. Otherwise, its output is LOW.
Check the truth table below to see the result for any combination of inputs.
Truth Table for the 3-input OR gate
First of all, you need a power supply voltage of 3 to 15V. Some versions of the chip support up to 20V. Check the datasheet of your version of the chip for exact values.
To be able to use any of the OR gates in the chip, you need to first connect the VDD pin to the positive supply terminal and the GND pin to the negative supply terminal.
The A, B, and C pins are the inputs to the three OR gates in the IC.
The Q pins are the outputs from the OR gates.
CD4075 Example Circuit – RGB LED Color Switcher

In the following circuit, the 555 timer creates a clock signal for the CD4017 counter. The first six outputs of the 4017 IC are connected to the 3-input OR gates in a way that turns rotates between six different colors.
A chip with 3-input OR gates such as the CD4075BE (U3)
You likely find the 4075 IC marked as CD4075, NTE4075, MC14075, HCF4075, TC4075, or HEF4075. Usually with a few extra characters at the end (Ex: CD4075BE).
This has to do with the manufacturer of the chip and the technology used. But the functionality and the pins are the same.
